startup.name: Soria
startup.one_liner: AI Financial Research Terminal built for Healthcare (and beyond)
startup.description: Soria is an AI native financial terminal for sector specialist investors, starting with healthcare. Agents convert public and private sources into an always on financial model reviewed by domain experts and delivered to hedge funds, banks and asset managers via terminal UI, MCP, API, warehouse sync and a research feed. Three person team in New York.

yc_acceptance.basis: Note only: already accepted to YC Spring 2026. Prior of about 1 percent for a random applicant (yc_acceptance.md) is not informative, so the real work is in the ladder.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: Not applicable because the company was accepted. A reviewer would most plausibly worry that the product pitch is broad, that AlphaSense, Bloomberg and many AI research startups already sell to funds, and that a three person team cannot build a proprietary data layer. Because acceptance is already a fact in this test, the estimate is a placeholder and the forecast value sits in the funding ladder that follows.

ladder.why_it_fails: Seed stalls if funds only pilot and do not pay, because buyers are slow and demand evidence of accuracy. Analogs Trata and Dataglade show years without a confirmed round after their batches. Domain expert review adds cost that may scare seed investors. Investors at this step want proof that growth, retention and margins hold up against better funded rivals, and a weak showing on any of them ends the path here, as the analogs listed in this evaluation show.

outcomes.why_it_fails: Most likely a stall or an acquisition by a data provider such as a larger research platform, because buyers consolidate vendors and a three person team faces large incumbents with distribution. A meaningful exit needs a durable lead in a category where rivals can copy features and raise more money, and most companies in the reference cohort stay small, are acquired cheaply or stop operating before that point.

technical_complexity.rationale: Ingestion pipelines and agents over filings are buildable by a small team. Building accurate sector models, licensing private sources and passing fund security reviews is hard and expensive, and reliability matters because mistakes cost money.

takeover_risk.rationale: Incumbents have data and distribution and model labs are adding finance agents; a bundled copy could arrive within a year, so the proprietary data layer must be the defense.

brand.name_check: python3 -I scripts/name_features.py --score "Soria" --era 2022+: 5 characters, 2 syllables, suffix coinage ending in ia
weaknesses: Not tied to finance or healthcare, and an ia ending is common
brand.rationale: Short coined names are common for YC finance companies and rarely decide outcomes; sales quality and data trust matter far more, as in the research terminal category.

narrative.headline: Real budgets but a crowded buyer market; a seed is plausible and later rounds depend on a proprietary data edge.
narrative.general_summary: Soria sells an AI research terminal to sector funds, starting in healthcare. Funds pay well and AI research is a funded category, so a seed is more likely than not. The weak points are a three person team, strong incumbents and similar YC peers that stalled after seed. If the proprietary data layer proves real and two or three funds pay, the path to a Series A is credible. The forecast treats the day one description as the best case, anchors on the 2022 to 2024 cohort of researched YC companies, and widens the uncertainty because funding data for recent batches is incomplete and right censored.
